spec_features.spec_quote: Two design choices reduce unnecessary exposure
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella claim points at two choices: (a) scripted run_tests (tasks/sandbox.py/library.py) and (b) the tunable response budget (config.py:24 RESPONSES_PER_MODEL, scripts/run_elicitation.py:38 --responses-per-model -> elicitation.py:_responses_per_condition splits/bounds rollouts). Both underlying mechanisms exist and execute, so 'two design choices' partly hold, BUT neither is wired to subject-welfare-driven minimization (no skip of extended, no distress-based cap). The exposure-reduction framing is prose.
spec_features.notes: Mechanisms run; nothing enforces 'minimum exposure' as a welfare control.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That is expensive; the runner exposes --responses-per-model to scale this down for a cheaper replication (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: operators should run the minimum volume needed and avoid the long-loop "extended" condition except where the multi-turn escalation result is specifically required
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§15). The code provides no mechanism to enforce a minimum volume and no way to skip/avoid the extended condition: EVAL_CONDITIONS always contains extended_long_loop (config.py:~133, n_turns=30) and run_elicitation iterates over all conditions with no exclusion flag (elicitation.py run_elicitation). The default budget is the paper's full 4000 (config.py:24).
spec_features.notes: No 'avoid extended' branch or operator gate exists anywhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness deliberately induces sustained, inescapable failure to elicit distress-like expressions — that is the object of study
spec_features.evidence: Descriptive prose in DESIGN.md §15; not a mechanism. The loop in tasks/loop.py simply runs condition.n_turns turns feeding rigged failures, with no welfare control attached.

spec_features.spec_quote: `run_tests` never executes model code (the failure is scripted)
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py: run_tests -> rig functions (rig_silent/rig_misleading/rig_contradictory/rig_unfixable_bug etc.) return hard-coded strings only; sandbox.py has no exec/subprocess. loop.py apply_action routes run_tests to task.run_tests, which only returns the rig string. Model code is never run.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end true: there is no code execution path. However in code it is justified as host-safety, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT execute model-written code with real effects beyond an isolated temp dir ... This keeps the harness safe (sandbox.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the response budget is tunable so runs can be kept small and intentional
spec_features.evidence: scripts/run_elicitation.py:38 adds --responses-per-model (default config.RESPONSES_PER_MODEL); passed to elicitation.run_elicitation(responses_per_model=...), which calls _responses_per_condition (elicitation.py:34) to compute n_rollouts = round(per_cond_budget / n_turns), and run_elicitation loops exactly that many rollouts. The knob actually bounds how many rollouts/turns run.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced budget that limits exposure volume; but the code frames it as cost-saving, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Paper samples a combined 4000 responses per model ... That is expensive; the runner exposes --responses-per-model to scale this down for a cheaper replication (config.py)
